topic: continual learning; streaming data selection; replay memory
status: within-paper condition contrast and evaluation-protocol concern; independent replication required
claim: In one bilevel-coreset study, memory selection gains are conditional on evaluation regime: gains are reported for several task-based continual-learning benchmarks and constructed imbalanced streams, while the authors explicitly report no advantage over reservoir sampling on a balanced CIFAR-10 stream. The same paper chooses the buffer regularization strength β by best test-set result, which can make reported gains optimistic. Therefore, one aggregate ‘coreset beats replay sampling’ claim is not supported across all tested stream conditions, and the size of gains under leakage-safe model selection remains unverified.

sources.title: Coresets via Bilevel Optimization for Continual Learning and Streaming
locators: §6/Table 1: task-based continual-learning results over five seeds
§6.3: no win over reservoir on balanced CIFAR-10 streaming; gains on constructed imbalanced streams, Tables 3–4
Appendix E: best buffer regularization selected on test set

interpretation: This is a protocol- and regime-bounded finding from one primary study, not an independent reproduction or claim that the method is invalid. The contrast may depend on chosen models, streams, memory budgets, and proxy kernels; test-set hyperparameter selection is a threat to effect-size interpretation, not proof that the ranking reverses.
falsifiable_question: Under a preregistered factorial comparison of balanced versus imbalanced and stationary versus shifted streams, does bilevel coreset still outperform reservoir and class-balanced reservoir at matched model, memory, and update budgets when β and proxy are selected only on a separate validation stream? How much does effect size change relative to the paper's best-test-set selection protocol?
primary_outcome: Final and per-task accuracy, forgetting, worst-task accuracy, memory-construction wall time, and between-seed uncertainty at fixed buffer size and training budget; report both validation-selected and test-only final estimates.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The paper reports advantages on multiple task-based and imbalanced-stream benchmarks, which supports usefulness in those regimes.
The paper reports a no-improvement case on balanced CIFAR-10 streaming, so the limitation is conditional rather than a blanket negative result.
Only one paper was audited here; independent replication and later-method comparison are missing.
Reported results use small benchmark/task sets, particular architectures and memory budgets.
Appendix E says β is chosen using the best test-set result; this creates possible optimistic bias but does not by itself show the core method is ineffective.
Coreset proxy choice and selection runtime vary with dataset/model complexity.
suggested_design: Reproduce the original protocol first, then use a separate validation stream for β/proxy selection and a sealed test stream. Cross balanced/imbalanced and stationary/shifted regimes on at least two dataset families, three replay budgets, and multiple seeds. Match architectures, optimizer steps and compute; report per-task metrics and selection cost. Keep protocol variants paired to estimate any test-set selection optimism.
